steps.instruction: Take close photos of both sides of the engine: wiring and hose routing, clamps and ties, the clutch cable path, the carburetor vent and overflow hoses and the throttle cable. These are your refit map. Label one bag per area: exhaust, seat and tank, carburetor, wiring, drive side, clutch side, mounts.
steps.title: Photograph the bike before you start
verification: Photos clearly show every lead, hose and cable route on both sides.
Bags are labelled.

steps.instruction: Lift the bike onto a stand under the frame so both wheels are off the floor, and strap the frame down. The swingarm pivot shaft runs through the engine on this bike, so the rear end loses its support when the shaft comes out later. Do not use the sidestand for this job.
steps.title: Put the bike on a stand and strap it
verification: Both wheels clear of the floor.
Bike does not rock when pushed at the bars and seat.

steps.instruction: With the bike level, set a pan under the engine and remove the transmission oil drain bolt and the oil filler cap. Let it drain fully. Look at the oil and wipe the drain bolt: note any metal, glitter or a milky look. The drain bolt goes back later at 23 N·m (17 lb·ft) with a new aluminum washer.
steps.title: Drain the transmission oil
verification: Oil fully drained.
Condition of the oil recorded (clean, glitter, chunks, milky).

steps.instruction: Only with the engine cold: lay a thick rag over the radiator cap, turn it slowly to the first stop to release any pressure, then take it off. Remove the coolant drain bolt on the water pump cover and catch the coolant; it can spray sideways, so hold the pan close. Keep the drain bolt for refit (new copper washer, 10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft).
steps.title: Drain the coolant
verification: Coolant drained into a pan and disposed of properly.
Coolant color and any oil film noted.

steps.instruction: Remove the seat, both side covers (they slide backward because their tabs sit in the air filter case) and both radiator shrouds. Check the fuel cock is off, disconnect the fuel hose at the carburetor and cap it, then remove the tank mounting bolts and lift the tank off with its breather hose.
steps.title: Remove the seat, side covers, shrouds and fuel tank
verification: Tank off and stored upright away from sparks.
Fuel hose capped; no fuel dripping.

steps.instruction: Remove the right side cover, the silencer bolts and silencer, then unhook the two exhaust tension springs and remove the exhaust pipe bolts and stay bolts. Lift the pipe off the cylinder.
steps.title: Remove the silencer and exhaust pipe
verification: Pipe and silencer off with all washers and collars bagged.
Exhaust port and pipe joint checked for damage; replacement seal noted if needed.

steps.instruction: Loosen the clamps on the carburetor joint and the air filter case joint. Free the throttle cable at the carburetor (or lift off the carburetor top with the slide still on the cable and tape the slide so it cannot be damaged), unplug any leads from the carburetor, pull the vent and overflow hoses from their clips, and twist the carburetor out. Plug the intake with a clean rag.
steps.title: Remove the carburetor
verification: Carburetor off, kept upright so the float bowl does not spill.
Intake opening covered.

steps.instruction: Loosen the radiator hose clamps and pull the hoses from the cylinder head and the water pump. If a radiator or hose still blocks the engine, remove the radiator guard and radiator bolts and lift that radiator away, protecting the fins.
steps.title: Disconnect the cooling hoses
verification: No coolant hose connects the engine to the frame any more.
Radiator fins protected.

steps.instruction: Disconnect the clutch cable at the engine side. Pull off the spark plug cap. Unplug the ignition (CDI magneto) lead, and the throttle position sensor, fuel-cut solenoid valve and neutral switch leads. Cut cable ties only where you have photos, and move every lead clear of the engine. Unhook the YPVS breather hose if it is routed to the frame.
steps.title: Disconnect the clutch cable and wiring
verification: Every lead, hose and cable between engine and frame is free (check both sides twice).

steps.instruction: Remove the drive sprocket cover and chain guide. Bend back the tab of the lock washer, put the transmission in gear and hold the rear brake while a helper loosens the drive sprocket nut. Remove the nut, lock washer and sprocket, and lift the chain off.
steps.title: Remove the drive sprocket
verification: Sprocket, nut and lock washer bagged; lock washer to be replaced if the tab is cracked.

steps.instruction: Remove the brake pedal bolt and take off the brake pedal and its return spring. Do not press the master cylinder pushrod while the pedal is off.
steps.title: Remove the brake pedal
verification: Pedal, spring and bolt bagged.

steps.instruction: Set a jack or wooden block under the engine so the mounts are unloaded. Check again from both sides that nothing still links the engine to the frame.
steps.title: Take the engine weight
verification: Engine weight supported; mounts move freely by hand.

steps.instruction: Remove the upper engine bracket bolts and nuts and lift off both brackets, then the front and lower engine mounting bolts and nuts. Keep each bolt with its nut and note which way it was inserted.
steps.title: Remove the engine brackets and mounting bolts
verification: Brackets and bolts bagged and labelled by position.

steps.instruction: Remove the pivot shaft nut. Drive the pivot shaft out with a soft drift while a helper holds the swingarm. As the shaft leaves the engine, push a round bar of the same diameter in from the other side so the swingarm stays held in the frame.
steps.title: Pull the swingarm pivot shaft
verification: Pivot shaft out and kept clean.
Swingarm held by the dummy bar and does not drop.

steps.instruction: Lift the engine until its front mount clears the frame bracket, then tilt it toward the kickstarter side and bring it out upward at an angle so the top mount does not catch the frame. Watch for snagging wires and hoses while it moves. Set it on a clean bench or engine stand.
steps.title: Lift the engine out
verification: Engine out with no damaged leads, hoses or frame paint.
Engine secured on the bench so it cannot tip.

steps.instruction: With the engine out, check the frame mounts and engine brackets for cracks and elongated holes, and check the pivot shaft for bending by rolling it on a flat surface. Record anything found.
steps.title: Check the empty chassis
verification: Mounts, brackets and pivot shaft checked; findings recorded.

prerequisites: Engine fully assembled with all covers on.
Frame, mounts and pivot shaft checked and clean.
Torque wrench available.

required_parts.name: Molybdenum disulfide grease
New aluminum washer for the transmission oil drain bolt
New copper washer for the coolant drain bolt
Transmission oil: Motor oil SAE 10W-40, API service SG or higher, JASO MA
required_parts.purpose: 0.80 L (0.85 US qt) after an engine rebuild.

required_parts.name: Coolant: ethylene glycol antifreeze made for aluminum engines, mixed 1:1 with distilled water
New lock washer for the drive sprocket nut if the old one is cracked

required_tools.name: Metric sockets, wrenches and hex keys

steps.instruction: Clean the pivot shaft and coat it with molybdenum disulfide grease. Check the swingarm pivot seals are seated.
steps.title: Clean and grease the pivot shaft
verification: Shaft clean, straight and greased.

steps.instruction: With a helper, bring the engine in from the right side, tilted toward the kickstarter side, and lift it into position on the jack. Keep all leads and hoses clear so nothing is trapped.
steps.title: Lift the engine into the frame
verification: Engine sitting in the frame with no pinched leads or hoses.

steps.instruction: Line up the swingarm and engine pivot holes. Push the pivot shaft in from the side that pushes the dummy bar out, so the swingarm never drops. Fit the nut finger tight.
steps.title: Fit the pivot shaft
verification: Pivot shaft through swingarm and engine; dummy bar out.

steps.instruction: Fit the lower and front engine mounting bolts with their nuts, then both upper engine brackets with their bolts and nuts, all finger tight, in the directions you recorded.
steps.title: Fit the mounting bolts and brackets
verification: All mounting hardware in place and finger tight.

steps.instruction: Remove the jack, then tighten: pivot shaft nut 85 N·m (61 lb·ft); lower engine mounting nut 64 N·m (46 lb·ft); front engine mounting nut 64 N·m (46 lb·ft); engine bracket nuts, upper side 34 N·m (24 lb·ft); engine bracket nut, lower side 64 N·m (46 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the engine mounts
verification: Each nut torqued and marked with paint.

steps.instruction: Fit the brake pedal and return spring, grease the pivot and tighten the brake pedal bolt to 26 N·m (19 lb·ft). Check the pedal returns by itself.
steps.title: Refit the brake pedal
verification: Pedal moves freely and returns.

steps.instruction: Fit the chain onto the drive sprocket, slide the sprocket on, fit the lock washer and nut. Hold the rear brake with the transmission in gear and tighten the drive sprocket nut to 75 N·m (54 lb·ft), then bend the lock washer tab against a flat of the nut. Fit the chain guide and the sprocket cover (5 N·m / 3.6 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the drive sprocket
verification: Nut torqued and lock washer tab bent.
Cover fitted.

steps.instruction: Route and plug in the ignition (CDI magneto) lead, and the throttle position sensor, fuel-cut solenoid valve and neutral switch leads exactly as in your photos and refit the cable ties. Refit the spark plug cap. Fit the clutch cable at the engine with its O-ring greased and pushed in straight so the O-ring is not pinched.
steps.title: Reconnect wiring and the clutch cable
verification: All leads plugged in and clipped as in the photos.
Clutch cable fitted; lever pulls cleanly.

steps.instruction: Refit any radiator you removed (10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft; guards 10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft), connect every hose to the cylinder head and water pump and tighten the hose clamps to 2 N·m (1.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Reconnect the cooling system
verification: Every hose pushed fully on and clamped.

steps.instruction: Remove the rag from the intake. Fit the carburetor into the joints so its locating projection sits in the slot of the carburetor joint and the carburetor stands upright, then tighten the joint clamps snugly. Refit the throttle cable or carburetor top, reconnect any carburetor leads, and route the vent and overflow hoses as in your photos.
steps.title: Refit the carburetor
verification: Carburetor straight and firmly clamped.
Throttle opens fully and snaps shut with the bars turned lock to lock.

steps.instruction: Fit the exhaust pipe to the cylinder, hook on both tension springs, and tighten the exhaust pipe bolts (front 14 N·m / 10 lb·ft, rear 12 N·m / 8.7 lb·ft) and exhaust stay bolts (front 25 N·m / 18 lb·ft, rear 12 N·m / 8.7 lb·ft). Fit the silencer with its collars and washers and tighten the silencer bolts to 12 N·m (8.7 lb·ft). Refit the right side cover.
steps.title: Refit the exhaust and silencer
verification: Pipe seated with no gap at the cylinder; springs hooked.
All exhaust fasteners torqued.

steps.instruction: Fit the fuel tank with its breather hose and connect the fuel hose. Tighten the tank bolts at the frame bosses to 20 N·m (14 lb·ft) and the other tank bolts to 10 N·m (7.2 lb·ft). Fit the shrouds (7 N·m / 5.1 lb·ft), side covers (7 N·m / 5.1 lb·ft) and the seat (19 N·m / 13 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the fuel tank, shrouds, side covers and seat
verification: No fuel leak at the hose or fuel cock with the cock turned on.

steps.instruction: Fit the drain bolt with a new aluminum washer (23 N·m / 17 lb·ft). Fill with motor oil SAE 10W-40, API service SG or higher, JASO MA: 0.80 L (0.85 US qt) after the engine has been apart (0.75 L / 0.79 US qt for a plain oil change). With the bike upright and level, remove the oil check bolt: oil should just flow out; if not, add oil until it does. Refit the check bolt (10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft) and the filler cap.
steps.title: Fill the transmission oil
verification: Correct amount added and level confirmed at the check bolt.
No leaks.

steps.instruction: Fit the coolant drain bolt with a new copper washer (10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft). Fill the radiator with a 1:1 mix of antifreeze for aluminum engines and distilled water. The full system holds 1.20 L (1.27 US qt). Squeeze the hoses to push air out, top up to the filler neck and fit the radiator cap.
steps.title: Fill the coolant
verification: Coolant to the top of the filler neck.
No leaks at hoses, drain bolt or water pump.

steps.instruction: Set clutch lever free play to 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in) and throttle grip free play to 3.0–5.0 mm (0.12–0.20 in). Set drive chain slack to 48.0–58.0 mm (1.89–2.28 in) with the bike on the stand.
steps.title: Set the controls and chain
verification: Clutch, throttle and chain within range.

steps.instruction: Go round the bike with your photos and bags: every bag should be empty. Check every hose clamp, lead and cable tie again, and that the bars turn lock to lock without pulling any cable or hose.
steps.title: Final walk-round
verification: All bags empty.
Nothing pulls or binds at full lock.

title: Top end: tear down, measure and rebuild the cylinder, piston and power valve
completeness: Covers head and cylinder removal, the YPVS power valve parts in the cylinder, piston, pin, ring and small end bearing checks with their limits, and reassembly with all top-end torques.
critical_stop_conditions: Cylinder bore beyond its wear limit of 66.500 mm (2.6181 in): the cylinder is replaced with a matched piston and rings.
Vertical scores on the cylinder wall or piston: replace the cylinder and fit a new piston and rings as a set.
Blue heat marks or grooves on the piston pin: replace the pin and find out why it ran hot (premix ratio or fuel) before running the engine.
The set pin is not in place when the push rod bolt is turned: stop; the power valve parts can be damaged.
A piston pin clip falls into the crankcase: stop and recover it before going further, even if it means splitting the cases.
Stud threads pull or strip: repair the thread before torquing.
entry_state: Yamaha YZ250X with the engine either in the frame or on the bench, cold, coolant drained, seat, fuel tank, exhaust and carburetor removed.
excluded: YPVS governor in the right crankcase cover (bottom-end guide)
exit_state: Cylinder head, cylinder, power valve and piston measured, rebuilt and torqued; engine ready for its carburetor, exhaust and coolant. If the cases are being split, continue with the bottom-end guide before refitting the top end; otherwise go to the first start and break-in guide.
prerequisites: Engine cold and coolant drained.
Area around the head and cylinder washed so no dirt falls into the crankcase.
Seat, fuel tank, exhaust pipe and carburetor removed (see the engine removal guide for each item).

New piston pin clips
New power valve cover gasket and power valve housing gasket
Piston, rings, pin and small end bearing as measured
required_parts.purpose: Replaced when out of limit or damaged; piston and rings go in as a set.

required_parts.name: Engine oil (two-stroke oil is fine)
required_parts.purpose: Assembly lubricant for piston, rings, pin and bearing.

required_parts.name: Lithium-soap-based grease and molybdenum disulfide oil
required_parts.purpose: O-rings, seal lips and power valve parts.

required_tools.name: Outside micrometer (50 to 75 mm range for this piston)
The set pin from the bike's tool kit for the power valve push rod bolt
Clean rags to block the crankcase opening

steps.instruction: With seat, tank, exhaust and carburetor off and the coolant drained, disconnect the radiator hose from the cylinder head and remove the spark plug. Remove the upper engine brackets. Blow loose dirt off the head and cylinder base so nothing can fall in.
steps.title: Prepare and clean the work area
verification: Head and cylinder area clean; plug out; brackets off.

steps.instruction: Loosen the cylinder head nuts a quarter turn at a time in a crisscross pattern until all are loose, then remove them with their copper washers. Lift off the head, the O-rings and the dowel pins.
steps.title: Remove the cylinder head
verification: Head off; O-rings and dowels bagged (O-rings and washers will be new).

steps.instruction: Remove the power valve housing bolts and take off the housing and its gasket from the side of the cylinder.
steps.title: Remove the power valve housing
verification: Housing off; gasket discarded.

steps.instruction: Fit the set pin from the bike's tool kit as shown on the tool before turning anything, then remove the push rod bolt and the push rod. Without the set pin the power valve parts can be damaged. Take the set pin out again afterwards.
steps.title: Remove the power valve push rod with the set pin fitted
verification: Set pin used and removed; push rod and bolt bagged.

steps.instruction: Remove the cylinder nuts, then lift the cylinder straight up off the piston while supporting the piston so it does not hit the case. Stuff clean rags into the crankcase opening around the connecting rod at once.
steps.title: Lift off the cylinder
verification: Cylinder off; crankcase opening fully covered.

steps.instruction: With the rags in place, remove one piston pin clip. Deburr the clip groove and the pin bore edge so the pin slides out. Push the pin out by hand; if it is still tight use the piston pin puller (YU-01304 / 90890-01304). Never hammer the pin. Remove the piston, the small end bearing and both piston rings (spread each ring at its gap by hand and lift it over the crown).
steps.title: Remove the piston
verification: Piston, pin, bearing and rings out; nothing dropped into the crankcase.

branches.condition: Warpage is 0.03 mm (0.0012 in) or less.
branches.label: Head is flat

steps.instruction: Scrape carbon from the combustion chamber with a rounded scraper, taking care of the spark plug threads. Check for damage and clean scale or rust from the water jacket. Lay a straightedge across the gasket face in several directions and measure warpage with feeler gauges. Limit: 0.03 mm (0.0012 in).
steps.title: Clean and check the cylinder head
verification: Warpage recorded.

steps.instruction: Put 400 to 600 grit wet sandpaper on a surface plate and resurface the head in a figure-eight pattern, turning the head every few strokes so it stays even. Measure again; replace the head if it cannot be brought within the limit.
steps.title: Resurface the head if it is warped
verification: Warpage within limit after resurfacing, or head replaced.

steps.instruction: Clean the cylinder and look at the bore and the piston skirt in good light. Vertical scratches mean the cylinder must be replaced and a new piston and rings fitted with it.
steps.title: Inspect the cylinder wall
verification: Bore condition recorded.

steps.instruction: With a cylinder bore gauge, measure parallel to and at right angles to the crankshaft at three heights (six readings); the bore size is the largest of them. Standard: 66.400–66.414 mm (2.6142–2.6147 in); wear limit: 66.500 mm (2.6181 in). Work out taper as the largest top reading minus the largest middle reading: limit 0.050 mm (0.0020 in). The cylinder carries a size letter (A to D).
steps.title: Measure the bore
verification: All readings, the bore size, the taper and the cylinder letter recorded.

steps.instruction: Measure the piston skirt diameter with a micrometer at right angles to the pin, 17.5 mm (0.69 in) from the stepped surface on the inside of the piston. Standard: 66.352–66.367 mm (2.6123–2.6129 in). The piston carries a size mark (A red, B orange, C green, D purple) that must match the cylinder letter.
steps.title: Measure the piston
verification: Piston diameter and size mark recorded.

steps.instruction: Clearance is the bore size minus the piston skirt diameter. Specification: 0.045–0.050 mm (0.0018–0.0020 in); limit 0.100 mm (0.0039 in). If it is out of limit, replace the cylinder and fit a piston and rings of the matching size mark as a set. A replacement cylinder cannot be ordered by size, so pick the piston to match the letter on the new cylinder.
steps.title: Work out piston-to-cylinder clearance
verification: Clearance calculated and recorded.

steps.instruction: Clean carbon out of the ring groove(s) and off the ring(s). Fit each ring in its groove and measure the gap between ring and groove side with a feeler gauge: top ring 0.030–0.065 mm (0.0012–0.0026 in) (limit 0.100 mm / 0.0039 in), second ring 0.030–0.065 mm (0.0012–0.0026 in) (limit 0.100 mm / 0.0039 in). If it is beyond the limit, replace the piston and rings as a set.
steps.title: Measure ring side clearance
verification: Side clearance recorded for each ring.

steps.instruction: Push each ring into the bottom of the bore, where wear is least, and square it up with the piston crown. Measure the end gap with feeler gauges: standard 0.40–0.55 mm (0.0157–0.0217 in), top ring limit 0.95 mm (0.0374 in), second ring limit 0.95 mm (0.0374 in). Replace any ring beyond the limit.
steps.title: Measure ring end gap
verification: End gap recorded for each ring.

steps.instruction: Look at the pin and the small end bearing: blue heat marks mean replace them and check the fuel and premix you have been using. Measure the pin outside diameter (standard 17.995–18.000 mm / 0.7085–0.7087 in, limit 17.975 mm / 0.7077 in). Put the pin in the piston and feel for free play: there should be none; if there is, replace the pin and/or the piston. Then fit the small end bearing and pin in the connecting rod and feel again: noticeable free play means the rod, pin or bearing is worn and must be replaced as needed.
steps.title: Check the piston pin and its fit
verification: Pin diameter recorded; free play in piston and rod checked.

steps.instruction: Inspect the small end needle bearing. Any heat discoloration, flat or pitted needles, or a cage that is cracked means replace it.
steps.title: Check the small end bearing
verification: Bearing condition recorded.

steps.instruction: Remove the power valve cover, both side holders, thrust plate, power valve holder 1, power valve shaft, link lever, pulleys and springs, link rod, both power valves 2, power valve holder 2 and power valve 1, laying them out in order. Remove carbon from the valves and from the power valve bore in the cylinder with a rounded tool; do not scratch the aluminum.
steps.title: Strip and clean the power valve
verification: Parts laid out in order and decarbonized.

steps.instruction: Check power valves 1 and 2, both power valve holders, link lever, pulleys, shaft, link rod and washers for wear or damage, and springs 1 and 2 for breaks. Replace any worn part.
steps.title: Check the power valve parts
verification: Each part checked; replacements listed.

steps.instruction: Fit power valve 1 with its gouge facing up and coat it with molybdenum disulfide oil; fit power valve holder 2 and tighten its bolts to 6 N·m (4.3 lb·ft) with threadlocker. Fit both power valves 2 and the link rod with the cut-outs in its arm ends over the pins on the valves; fit the washers and tighten the link rod screws to 6 N·m (4.3 lb·ft). Fit the thrust plate before the shaft and tighten its screw to 6 N·m (4.3 lb·ft). Fit spring 1 to the link lever first and then into the cylinder with its stopper facing inward, then the pulleys (molybdenum disulfide oil in their grooves), spring 2, washer and the power valve shaft; grease the oil seal lip. Slide the shaft in with its cut lined up with the thrust plate, then turn it so the cut faces up. Fit power valve holder 1 and tighten the link lever bolt first (4 N·m / 2.9 lb·ft), then the pulley bolts (4 N·m / 2.9 lb·ft).
steps.title: Reassemble the power valve
verification: Every power valve fastener torqued.

steps.instruction: Turn the valve shaft by hand through its full travel. It must move smoothly and return under spring force with no sticking; if not, find the cause and fix it before going on.
steps.title: Check the power valve moves freely
verification: Smooth full travel and return.

steps.instruction: Grease new O-rings and fit both side holders with their projection facing up; tighten the side holder screws to 4 N·m (2.9 lb·ft). Fit the YPVS breather hose. Fit a new cover gasket with its cut facing down and printed side toward the cover, then the cover with its arrow pointing up; tighten the cover screws to 4 N·m (2.9 lb·ft).
steps.title: Close the power valve
verification: Cover and side parts torqued; arrow up.

steps.instruction: Fit both piston rings without scratching the piston, with each ring gap around its locating pin in the groove. Check each ring moves freely in its groove.
steps.title: Fit the ring(s) to the piston
verification: Ring gaps on their pins; rings free.

steps.instruction: Fit a new cylinder gasket with its printed side toward the crankcase and the dowel pins. Oil the crank bearings, the big end and its thrust washers through the case opening. Oil the small end bearing and slide it into the rod. With rags still blocking the crankcase, fit the piston with the mark on the crown pointing toward the exhaust port, oil the pin and push it in, then fit new pin clips. Turn each clip so its open end does not sit at the slot in the pin bore.
steps.title: Fit the piston to the connecting rod
verification: Piston mark toward exhaust.

Oil the spring, pawl pin and pawl and fit them to the shift lever, then fit the shift lever assembly and shift guide together; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Oil and fit the roller, washer and shift shaft.
steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
verification: Shift mechanism torqued; shaft returns to center.

steps.instruction: Fit the kick gear, washer and a new circlip, then the ratchet wheel with its punch mark lined up with the mark on the shaft (molybdenum disulfide grease in its bore), spring, washer and a new circlip. Fit the torsion spring (end in the shaft hole) and the spring guide. Grease the ratchet guide and stopper, oil the shaft, slide the assembly in so the stopper sits in the ratchet guide, then turn the torsion spring clockwise and hook it into its hole. Fit the kick idle gear depressed side out, washer and a new circlip.
steps.title: Refit the kickstarter
verification: Kick shaft springs back on its own.

steps.instruction: Fit the thrust plate, primary drive gear, governor drive gear and the washer with its chamfered side facing you; oil the bolt and start it.
steps.title: Refit the primary drive gear
verification: Bolt finger tight.

steps.instruction: If removed, fit the push lever shaft bearing, a new greased oil seal and the shaft. Fit a new copper washer and the push lever shaft bolt (6 N·m / 4.4 lb·ft). Oil and fit the thrust washer, spacer, bearing and primary driven gear, then the second thrust washer and the clutch boss. Fit a new lock washer and the boss nut; hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 75 N·m (55 lb·ft). Bend the lock washer tab up against the nut.
steps.title: Fit the clutch housing and boss
verification: Boss nut torqued; tab bent.

steps.instruction: Wedge the aluminum plate between the primary gears again and tighten the primary drive gear bolt to 55 N·m (41 lb·ft). Remove the plate.
steps.title: Torque the primary drive gear bolt
verification: Bolt torqued; plate removed.

steps.instruction: Oil the plates with transmission oil and stack them alternately on the boss, starting and ending with a friction plate. Fit push rod 2 with its smaller end toward you, then push rod 1 with its bearing, washer and new circlip, all oiled. Fit the pressure plate and the springs, and tighten the clutch spring bolts in stages, crisscross, to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Rebuild the clutch pack
verification: Plates stacked correctly; spring bolts torqued.

steps.instruction: Fit the dowel pins and a new gasket and fit the right cover. Make sure the governor and water pump gears mesh as the cover goes on. Tighten the cover bolts in stages, crisscross, to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Refit the kick crank boss, spring and ball. Fit the clutch cover with a new gasket or O-ring (10 N·m / 7.4 lb·ft). Fit the kickstarter lever (30 N·m / 22 lb·ft) so it sits close to, but not touching, the clutch cover mounting boss.
steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
verification: Covers torqued; kick lever clears everything and returns.

steps.instruction: Fit the stator with its bolts just snug. Clean the crank and rotor tapers, fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank axis, and slide the rotor on with its keyway on the key. Fit the washer and rotor nut and tighten to 56 N·m (41 lb·ft) while holding the rotor. Line the stator mark up with the timing mark on the case and tighten the stator bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the stator and rotor
verification: Rotor nut and stator bolts torqued; marks aligned.

steps.instruction: Route the magneto lead as before. Fit a new left cover gasket and the cover; tighten its fasteners in stages, crisscross, to 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft). Fit the shift pedal (12 N·m / 8.9 lb·ft) at its original position.

verification: Cover and pedal torqued.

steps.instruction: After the top end is back on, check the ignition timing with a dial gauge in the spark plug hole: from top dead center the rotor punch mark should line up with the stator mark at 0.18 mm (0.01 in) before top dead center. If it does not, loosen the stator bolts, move the stator, and retighten them to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
steps.title: Plan the ignition timing check
verification: Timing check noted for after the top end is fitted.

steps.instruction: Put the engine on its left side or in a stand on a clean bench, with a tray for each group of parts. Photograph each assembly before you take it apart.

verification: Engine stable; trays labelled: left side, clutch, right side, shift, case, gearbox.

steps.instruction: Remove the left crankcase cover fasteners and the cover with its gasket.
steps.title: Remove the left crankcase cover
verification: Cover off; rotor and stator visible.

steps.instruction: Hold the rotor with the rotor holding tool and remove the rotor nut and washer. Thread the flywheel puller (90890-01189 / YM-01189) into the rotor (it threads in counterclockwise) and pull the rotor off the taper. Take out the woodruff key.
steps.title: Remove the magneto rotor
verification: Rotor and key off; taper undamaged.

steps.instruction: Before loosening anything, mark the stator against the timing mark on the crankcase so the ignition timing goes back where it was. Remove the stator bolts and the stator with its lead.
steps.title: Mark and remove the stator
verification: Stator marked and off.

steps.instruction: Disconnect the clutch cable at the engine. Remove the clutch cover and gasket, loosen the clutch spring bolts in a crisscross pattern, and remove the springs, pressure plate and the friction and clutch plates in order. Pull out push rod 1 with its bearing and washer and push rod 2.
steps.title: Remove the clutch pack
verification: Plates kept in their stacking order.

steps.instruction: Bend back the lock washer tab. Hold the clutch boss with the clutch holder (90890-04199 / YM-91042) and remove the clutch boss nut. Do not use an impact wrench. Remove the lock washer, clutch boss and thrust washer, leaving the primary driven gear (clutch housing) in place for now.
steps.title: Remove the clutch boss
verification: Boss off; housing still meshed with the primary drive gear.

steps.instruction: Remove the kickstarter lever, the ball and spring and the kick crank boss, then the right crankcase cover bolts and the right cover with its gasket. The YPVS governor stays in the cover.
steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
verification: Cover off; governor fork and gears visible.

steps.instruction: Wedge a thin aluminum plate between the teeth of the primary drive gear and the primary driven gear so they cannot turn, and loosen the primary drive gear bolt.
steps.title: Loosen the primary drive gear bolt
verification: Bolt loose; no gear teeth damaged.

steps.instruction: Remove the primary driven gear with its bearing, spacer and thrust washer. Remove the primary drive gear bolt and washer, the governor drive gear, the primary drive gear and the thrust plate.
steps.title: Remove the primary gears
verification: Gears off and kept as a matched pair.

steps.instruction: Remove the circlip, washer and kick idle gear. Unhook the kickstarter torsion spring from its hole in the crankcase and pull out the kick shaft assembly.
steps.title: Remove the kickstarter
verification: Kickstarter parts laid out in order.

steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal and pull out the shift shaft with its roller and washer. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove the segment bolt and segment without knocking it. Remove the shift guide and shift lever assembly, then the stopper lever, holder and tension spring.
steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
verification: Shift parts laid out; segment not struck.

steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plates 2.90–3.10 mm (0.114–0.122 in) (wear limit 2.80 mm / 0.110 in). Check clutch plate warpage on a surface plate with a feeler gauge (limit 0.20 mm / 0.008 in). Measure clutch spring free length (standard 44.00 mm / 1.73 in, limit 41.80 mm / 1.65 in). Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface (bend limit 0.30 mm / 0.012 in). Check the housing dogs and boss splines for notches, the pressure plate for cracks, and the primary gears for wear and free play between them. Replace plates and springs as sets.
steps.title: Measure the clutch parts
verification: Every measurement recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: In the right cover, check the governor washers, collar, thrust bearing, balls and retainer for wear and the governor fork for damage. If you take it apart: grease the thrust bearing, oil the balls and retainer, compress the spring to fit the dowel pin into the retainer groove, and set the governor groove over the fork when it goes back in the cover.
steps.title: Check the YPVS governor
verification: Governor checked; condition recorded.

steps.instruction: Remove the holder, the neutral switch lead holder bolt and the crankcase bolts (7 × 50 mm, 1 × 60 mm, 3 × 70 mm), noting their positions. Fit the crankcase separating tool (90890-01135 / YU-01135-B) to the right case with suitable bolts, keep the tool body parallel to the case, and apply pressure while tapping alternately on the engine mounting boss and the transmission shafts with a soft hammer. Tap only on strong parts of the case, never on the joint face, and make sure the halves come apart evenly. If they stop, look for a bolt you missed.
steps.title: Split the crankcases
verification: Cases apart evenly with no damage to the joint faces.

steps.instruction: Lift the main axle, drive axle, shift drum and the three shift forks out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer. Note where every fork sits and which way it faces. Remove the collar.
steps.title: Remove the gearbox
verification: Gearbox out; fork positions photographed.

steps.instruction: Fit the crankcase separating tool (90890-01135 / YU-01135-B) with suitable bolts and press the crankshaft out of the case. Never drive the crankshaft out with a hammer.
steps.title: Remove the crankshaft
verification: Crank out without damage to the case.

branches.condition: Runout is 0.050 mm (0.0020 in) or less and width is within 59.95–60.00 mm (2.360–2.362 in).
branches.label: Crank within limits

steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks or centers, turn it slowly and measure runout with a dial gauge (limit 0.050 mm / 0.0020 in). Measure the crank assembly width across the flywheels (standard 59.95–60.00 mm / 2.360–2.362 in).
steps.title: Measure the crankshaft
verification: Runout and width recorded.

steps.instruction: A crank that is out of limit is replaced as an assembly. Do not reassemble the engine with it.
steps.title: Get a replacement crankshaft
verification: Replacement crankshaft on hand.

steps.instruction: Check each shift fork for wear and smooth movement on its guide; a bad fork means replacing the fork and the two gears beside it. Check the shift drum grooves and segment. With a centering device and dial gauge, measure main axle runout (limit 0.01 mm / 0.0004 in) and drive axle runout (limit 0.01 mm / 0.0004 in). Check every gear for blue heat marks, pitting and worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear moves freely on its shaft.
steps.title: Check the gearbox and shift parts
verification: Measurements and condition recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in mild solvent, remove all old sealant from the joint faces and blow the oil passages clear. Check for cracks. Before removing a bearing or seal, measure how deep it sits so the new one goes to the same depth. Press bearings out (a removed bearing is not reused) and press new ones in by the outer race, square, with engine oil on them. Fit new oil seals with their markings facing out and grease on the lips.
steps.title: Clean the cases and renew bearings and seals
verification: Cases clean and crack-free.
New bearings and seals at the original depths.

steps.instruction: Pull the crankshaft into the left case with the crankshaft installer pot, bolt and M12 adapter (90890-01274 / YU-90058 / 90890-01275 / YU-90060 / 90890-01278 / YU-90063). Hold the connecting rod at top dead center with one hand while you turn the installer nut with the other, until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Never hammer it in.
steps.title: Install the crankshaft
verification: Crank seated; rod at TDC; crank turns freely.

steps.instruction: Build each shaft in this order. Main axle: 5th pinion gear (25T), 3rd pinion gear (16T), Collar, 4th pinion gear (20T), 2nd pinion gear (15T). Drive axle: 2nd wheel gear (23T), 4th wheel gear (21T), 3rd wheel gear (21T), 5th wheel gear (21T), 1st wheel gear (27T), O-ring. Put molybdenum disulfide oil on the bore and end faces of free-running gears and inside sliding gears. Use new circlips with the sharp edge facing away from the washer and gear, and the circlip opening lined up with a spline groove.
steps.title: Build up the gearbox shafts
verification: Both shafts built in the correct order with new circlips.

steps.instruction: Grease the oil seal lip and fit the collar with its chamfered side toward the case. Fit the shift drum to the forks, then lower the whole gearbox into the left case together. Oil the bearings and guide bars.
steps.title: Fit the gearbox into the left case
verification: Forks in the right gears; gearbox seated.

steps.instruction: Turn the shift drum by hand through every gear while turning the main axle. Each gear must engage cleanly and both shafts must turn freely in neutral.

verification: All gears selected by hand; nothing binds.

steps.instruction: Clean both joint faces, fit a new O-ring to the right case and the dowel pins, and spread a thin even bead of Yamaha bond No. 1215 on the right case. Fit the right case onto the left with the connecting rod at top dead center and tap it down lightly with a soft hammer until the joint closes.

verification: Joint closed evenly all round.

steps.instruction: Fit the crankcase bolts in their positions (7 × 50 mm, 1 × 60 mm, 3 × 70 mm) and tighten them in stages, crisscross, to 14 N·m (10 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the crankcase bolts
verification: All case bolts torqued.
Crank spins freely and the gearbox still shifts.

steps.instruction: Fit the tension spring and holder (holder bolt 10 N·m / 7.4 lb·ft with threadlocker), the washer and the stopper lever (bolt 10 N·m / 7.4 lb·ft with threadlocker), roller lined up with the segment slot. Oil the spring, pawl pin and pawl and fit them to the shift lever, then fit the shift lever assembly and shift guide together; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Oil and fit the roller, washer and shift shaft.
steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
verification: Shift mechanism torqued; shaft returns to center.

steps.instruction: Fit the kick gear, washer and a new circlip, then the ratchet wheel with its punch mark lined up with the mark on the shaft (molybdenum disulfide grease in its bore), spring, washer and a new circlip. Fit the kick idle gear depressed side out, washer and a new circlip.
steps.title: Refit the kickstarter
verification: Kick shaft springs back on its own.

steps.instruction: Fit the thrust plate, primary drive gear, governor drive gear and the washer with its chamfered side facing you; oil the bolt and start it.
steps.title: Refit the primary drive gear
verification: Bolt finger tight.

steps.instruction: If removed, fit the push lever shaft bearing, a new greased oil seal and the shaft. Fit a new copper washer and the push lever shaft bolt (6 N·m / 4.4 lb·ft). Oil and fit the thrust washer, spacer, bearing and primary driven gear, then the second thrust washer and the clutch boss. Fit a new lock washer and the boss nut; hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 75 N·m (55 lb·ft). Bend the lock washer tab up against the nut.
steps.title: Fit the clutch housing and boss
verification: Boss nut torqued; tab bent.

steps.instruction: Wedge the aluminum plate between the primary gears again and tighten the primary drive gear bolt to 55 N·m (41 lb·ft). Remove the plate.
steps.title: Torque the primary drive gear bolt
verification: Bolt torqued; plate removed.

steps.instruction: Oil the plates with transmission oil and stack them alternately on the boss, starting and ending with a friction plate. Fit push rod 2 with its smaller end toward you, then push rod 1 with its bearing, washer and new circlip, all oiled. Fit the pressure plate and the springs, and tighten the clutch spring bolts in stages, crisscross, to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Rebuild the clutch pack
verification: Plates stacked correctly; spring bolts torqued.

Fit the kickstarter lever (30 N·m / 22 lb·ft) so it sits close to, but not touching, the clutch cover mounting boss.

verification: Covers torqued; kick lever clears everything and returns.

steps.title: Refit the stator and rotor
verification: Rotor nut and stator bolts torqued; marks aligned.

steps.instruction: Route the magneto lead as before. Fit a new left cover gasket and the cover; tighten its fasteners in stages, crisscross, to 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft). Fit the shift pedal (12 N·m / 8.9 lb·ft) at its original position.
steps.title: Refit the left cover and shift pedal
verification: Cover and pedal torqued.

steps.instruction: Support the crank on V-blocks or centers, turn it slowly and measure runout with a dial gauge (limit 0.050 mm / 0.0020 in). Measure the crank assembly width across the flywheels (standard 59.95–60.00 mm / 2.360–2.362 in).
steps.title: Measure the crankshaft
verification: Runout and width recorded.

steps.instruction: A crank that is out of limit is replaced as an assembly. Do not reassemble the engine with it.
steps.title: Get a replacement crankshaft
verification: Replacement crankshaft on hand.

steps.instruction: Check each shift fork for wear and smooth movement on its guide; a bad fork means replacing the fork and the two gears beside it. Check the shift drum grooves and segment. With a centering device and dial gauge, measure main axle runout (limit 0.01 mm / 0.0004 in) and drive axle runout (limit 0.01 mm / 0.0004 in). Check every gear for blue heat marks, pitting and worn or rounded dogs, and that each gear moves freely on its shaft.
steps.title: Check the gearbox and shift parts
verification: Measurements and condition recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: Wash both case halves in mild solvent, remove all old sealant from the joint faces and blow the oil passages clear. Check for cracks. Before removing a bearing or seal, measure how deep it sits so the new one goes to the same depth. Press bearings out (a removed bearing is not reused) and press new ones in by the outer race, square, with engine oil on them. Fit new oil seals with their markings facing out and grease on the lips.
steps.title: Clean the cases and renew bearings and seals
verification: Cases clean and crack-free.
New bearings and seals at the original depths.

steps.instruction: Pull the crankshaft into the left case with the crankshaft installer pot, bolt and M12 adapter (90890-01274 / YU-90058 / 90890-01275 / YU-90060 / 90890-01278 / YU-90063). Hold the connecting rod at top dead center with one hand while you turn the installer nut with the other, until the crank bottoms against the bearing. Never hammer it in.
steps.title: Install the crankshaft
verification: Crank seated; rod at TDC; crank turns freely.

steps.instruction: Build each shaft in this order. Main axle: 5th pinion gear (25T), 3rd pinion gear (16T), Collar, 4th pinion gear (20T), 2nd pinion gear (15T). Drive axle: 2nd wheel gear (23T), 4th wheel gear (21T), 3rd wheel gear (21T), 5th wheel gear (21T), 1st wheel gear (27T), O-ring. Put molybdenum disulfide oil on the bore and end faces of free-running gears and inside sliding gears. Use new circlips with the sharp edge facing away from the washer and gear, and the circlip opening lined up with a spline groove.
steps.title: Build up the gearbox shafts
verification: Both shafts built in the correct order with new circlips.

steps.instruction: Grease the oil seal lip and fit the collar with its chamfered side toward the case. Fit the shift forks to the shafts with molybdenum disulfide oil in their grooves: shift fork 1 (L) runs in the 4th wheel gear; shift fork 2 (C10) runs in the 3rd pinion gear; shift fork 3 (R) runs in the 5th wheel gear. Fit the shift drum to the forks, then lower the whole gearbox into the left case together. Oil the bearings and guide bars.
steps.title: Fit the gearbox into the left case
verification: Forks in the right gears; gearbox seated.

steps.instruction: Turn the shift drum by hand through every gear while turning the main axle. Each gear must engage cleanly and both shafts must turn freely in neutral.
steps.title: Check the gearbox shifts
verification: All gears selected by hand; nothing binds.

steps.instruction: Clean both joint faces, fit a new O-ring to the right case and the dowel pins, and spread a thin even bead of Yamaha bond No. 1215 on the right case. Fit the right case onto the left with the connecting rod at top dead center and tap it down lightly with a soft hammer until the joint closes.
steps.title: Close the crankcases
verification: Joint closed evenly all round.

steps.instruction: Fit the crankcase bolts in their positions (7 × 50 mm, 1 × 60 mm, 3 × 70 mm) and tighten them in stages, crisscross, to 14 N·m (10 lb·ft).
steps.title: Tighten the crankcase bolts
verification: All case bolts torqued.
Crank spins freely and the gearbox still shifts.

steps.instruction: Fit the tension spring and holder (holder bolt 10 N·m / 7.4 lb·ft with threadlocker), the washer and the stopper lever (bolt 10 N·m / 7.4 lb·ft with threadlocker), roller lined up with the segment slot. Push the stopper lever down and fit the segment with its notch on the shift drum pin; tighten the segment bolt to 30 N·m (22 lb·ft) without shocking it. Oil the spring, pawl pin and pawl and fit them to the shift lever, then fit the shift lever assembly and shift guide together; tighten the shift guide bolts with threadlocker to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Oil and fit the roller, washer and shift shaft.
steps.title: Refit the shift mechanism
verification: Shift mechanism torqued; shaft returns to center.

steps.instruction: Fit the kick gear, washer and a new circlip, then the ratchet wheel with its punch mark lined up with the mark on the shaft (molybdenum disulfide grease in its bore), spring, washer and a new circlip. Fit the torsion spring (end in the shaft hole) and the spring guide. Grease the ratchet guide and stopper, oil the shaft, slide the assembly in so the stopper sits in the ratchet guide, then turn the torsion spring clockwise and hook it into its hole. Fit the kick idle gear depressed side out, washer and a new circlip.
steps.title: Refit the kickstarter
verification: Kick shaft springs back on its own.

steps.instruction: Fit the thrust plate, primary drive gear, governor drive gear and the washer with its chamfered side facing you; oil the bolt and start it.
steps.title: Refit the primary drive gear
verification: Bolt finger tight.

steps.instruction: If removed, fit the push lever shaft bearing, a new greased oil seal and the shaft. Fit a new copper washer and the push lever shaft bolt (6 N·m / 4.4 lb·ft). Oil and fit the thrust washer, spacer, bearing and primary driven gear, then the second thrust washer and the clutch boss. Fit a new lock washer and the boss nut; hold the boss with the clutch holder and tighten the nut to 75 N·m (55 lb·ft). Bend the lock washer tab up against the nut.
steps.title: Fit the clutch housing and boss
verification: Boss nut torqued; tab bent.

steps.instruction: Wedge the aluminum plate between the primary gears again and tighten the primary drive gear bolt to 55 N·m (41 lb·ft). Remove the plate.
steps.title: Torque the primary drive gear bolt
verification: Bolt torqued; plate removed.

steps.instruction: Oil the plates with transmission oil and stack them alternately on the boss, starting and ending with a friction plate. Put the friction plates with black paint on their tabs at the innermost and outermost positions. Fit push rod 2 with its smaller end toward you, then push rod 1 with its bearing, washer and new circlip, all oiled. Fit the pressure plate and the springs, and tighten the clutch spring bolts in stages, crisscross, to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft).
steps.title: Rebuild the clutch pack
verification: Plates stacked correctly; spring bolts torqued.

steps.instruction: Fit the dowel pins and a new gasket and fit the right cover. Make sure the governor and water pump gears mesh as the cover goes on. Tighten the cover bolts in stages, crisscross, to 10 N·m (7.4 lb·ft). Refit the kick crank boss, spring and ball. Fit the clutch cover with a new gasket or O-ring (10 N·m / 7.4 lb·ft). Fit the kickstarter lever (30 N·m / 22 lb·ft) so it sits close to, but not touching, the clutch cover mounting boss.
steps.title: Refit the right crankcase cover
verification: Covers torqued; kick lever clears everything and returns.

steps.instruction: Fit the stator with its bolts just snug. Clean the crank and rotor tapers, fit the woodruff key with its flat face parallel to the crank axis, and slide the rotor on with its keyway on the key. Fit the washer and rotor nut and tighten to 56 N·m (41 lb·ft) while holding the rotor. Line the stator mark up with the timing mark on the case and tighten the stator bolts to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
steps.title: Refit the stator and rotor
verification: Rotor nut and stator bolts torqued; marks aligned.

steps.instruction: Route the magneto lead as before. Fit a new left cover gasket and the cover; tighten its fasteners in stages, crisscross, to 5 N·m (3.7 lb·ft). Fit the shift pedal (12 N·m / 8.9 lb·ft) at its original position.
steps.title: Refit the left cover and shift pedal
verification: Cover and pedal torqued.

steps.instruction: After the top end is back on, check the ignition timing with a dial gauge in the spark plug hole: from top dead center the rotor punch mark should line up with the stator mark at 0.18 mm (0.01 in) before top dead center. If it does not, loosen the stator bolts, move the stator, and retighten them to 7 N·m (5.2 lb·ft).
steps.title: Plan the ignition timing check
verification: Timing check noted for after the top end is fitted.

title: Bottom end: split the cases and rebuild the crankshaft, gearbox and clutch
completeness: Covers the magneto, clutch, primary drive, kickstarter, shift mechanism and YPVS governor, splitting the cases, crankshaft and gearbox checks with their limits, bearing and seal renewal, and reassembly.
critical_stop_conditions: Crankshaft runout over 0.050 mm (0.0020 in) or crank width out of 59.95–60.00 mm (2.360–2.362 in): the crankshaft assembly is replaced.
Main axle or drive axle runout over 0.01 mm (0.0004 in): replace that axle.
The cases do not separate evenly with the puller: stop, look for a hidden bolt or fitting, and never pry on the joint face.
Do not use an impact wrench on the clutch boss nut, and do not hammer the crankshaft in or out.
Do not shock the shift segment; the stopper lever can be damaged.
Cracks in a case half, a spun bearing bore or damaged threads: stop; the case must be repaired or replaced.
entry_state: Yamaha YZ250X engine out of the frame on a bench, transmission oil and coolant drained, cylinder head, cylinder and piston removed (top-end guide).
excluded: Crankshaft rebuilding (the crank is replaced as an assembly when out of limit)
exit_state: Cases closed on a checked crankshaft and gearbox with new bearings and seals as needed; clutch, kickstarter, shift mechanism, governor and ignition rebuilt to torque. Refit the top end (the top-end guide), then the engine.
prerequisites: Engine clean on a bench with the top end removed.
Rags stuffed in the crankcase mouth.
Every part laid out in order on a clean tray as it comes off.

required_parts.name: New crankcase gaskets, cover gaskets, O-rings and oil seals
New crankcase bearings as needed
required_parts.purpose: A bearing removed from the case is never reused.

required_parts.name: New lock washer for the clutch boss nut, new circlips
Yamaha bond No. 1215 (90890-85505) or equivalent
Molybdenum disulfide oil and grease, lithium-soap-based grease, medium threadlocker
Transmission oil: Motor oil SAE 10W-40 type SG or higher

required_tools.name: A thin aluminum plate to lock the primary gears
Crankcase separating tool (90890-01135 / YU-01135-B) with suitable bolts
Dial gauge with V-blocks or centers
Feeler gauges and a surface plate
Bearing drivers and a press or heat source for case bearings

steps.instruction: Put the engine on its left side or in a stand on a clean bench, with a tray for each group of parts. Photograph each assembly before you take it apart.
steps.title: Set up the engine and a parts layout
verification: Engine stable; trays labelled: left side, clutch, right side, shift, case, gearbox.

steps.instruction: Remove the left crankcase cover fasteners and the cover with its gasket.
steps.title: Remove the left crankcase cover
verification: Cover off; rotor and stator visible.

steps.instruction: Hold the rotor with the rotor holding tool (90890-04195) and remove the rotor nut and washer. Thread the flywheel puller (90890-01189 / YM-01189) into the rotor (it threads in counterclockwise) and pull the rotor off the taper. Take out the woodruff key.
steps.title: Remove the magneto rotor
verification: Rotor and key off; taper undamaged.

steps.instruction: Before loosening anything, mark the stator against the timing mark on the crankcase so the ignition timing goes back where it was. Remove the stator bolts and the stator with its lead.
steps.title: Mark and remove the stator
verification: Stator marked and off.

steps.instruction: Disconnect the clutch cable at the engine. Remove the clutch cover and gasket, loosen the clutch spring bolts in a crisscross pattern, and remove the springs, pressure plate and the friction and clutch plates in order. Pull out push rod 1 with its bearing and washer and push rod 2.
steps.title: Remove the clutch pack
verification: Plates kept in their stacking order.

steps.instruction: Bend back the lock washer tab. Hold the clutch boss with the clutch holder (90890-04199 / YM-91042) and remove the clutch boss nut. Do not use an impact wrench. Remove the lock washer, clutch boss and thrust washer, leaving the primary driven gear (clutch housing) in place for now.
steps.title: Remove the clutch boss
verification: Boss off; housing still meshed with the primary drive gear.

steps.instruction: Remove the kickstarter lever, the ball and spring and the kick crank boss, then the right crankcase cover bolts and the right cover with its gasket. The YPVS governor stays in the cover.
steps.title: Remove the right crankcase cover
verification: Cover off; governor fork and gears visible.

steps.instruction: Wedge a thin aluminum plate between the teeth of the primary drive gear and the primary driven gear so they cannot turn, and loosen the primary drive gear bolt.
steps.title: Loosen the primary drive gear bolt
verification: Bolt loose; no gear teeth damaged.

steps.instruction: Remove the primary driven gear with its bearing, spacer and thrust washer. Remove the primary drive gear bolt and washer, the governor drive gear, the primary drive gear and the thrust plate.
steps.title: Remove the primary gears
verification: Gears off and kept as a matched pair.

steps.instruction: Remove the circlip, washer and kick idle gear. Unhook the kickstarter torsion spring from its hole in the crankcase and pull out the kick shaft assembly.
steps.title: Remove the kickstarter
verification: Kickstarter parts laid out in order.

steps.instruction: Remove the shift pedal and pull out the shift shaft with its roller and washer. Turn the segment counterclockwise until it stops and remove the segment bolt and segment without knocking it. Remove the shift guide and shift lever assembly, then the stopper lever, holder and tension spring.
steps.title: Remove the shift mechanism
verification: Shift parts laid out; segment not struck.

steps.instruction: Measure each friction plate at four points: friction plates 1 2.92–3.08 mm (0.115–0.121 in) (limit 2.82 mm / 0.111 in) and friction plates 2 2.90–3.10 mm (0.114–0.122 in) (limit 2.80 mm / 0.110 in). Check clutch plate warpage on a surface plate with a feeler gauge (limit 0.20 mm / 0.008 in). Measure clutch spring free length (standard 44.00 mm / 1.73 in, limit 41.80 mm / 1.65 in). Roll push rod 2 on a flat surface (bend limit 0.30 mm / 0.012 in). Check the housing dogs and boss splines for notches, the pressure plate for cracks, and the primary gears for wear and free play between them. Replace plates and springs as sets.
steps.title: Measure the clutch parts
verification: Every measurement recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: In the right cover, check the governor washers, collar, thrust bearing, balls and retainer for wear and the governor fork for damage. If you take it apart: grease the thrust bearing, oil the balls and retainer, compress the spring to fit the dowel pin into the retainer groove, and set the governor groove over the fork when it goes back in the cover.
steps.title: Check the YPVS governor
verification: Governor checked; condition recorded.

steps.instruction: Remove the holder, the neutral switch lead holder bolt and the crankcase bolts (7 × 50 mm, 1 × 60 mm, 3 × 70 mm), noting their positions. Fit the crankcase separating tool (90890-01135 / YU-01135-B) to the right case with suitable bolts, keep the tool body parallel to the case, and apply pressure while tapping alternately on the engine mounting boss and the transmission shafts with a soft hammer. Tap only on strong parts of the case, never on the joint face, and make sure the halves come apart evenly. If they stop, look for a bolt you missed.
steps.title: Split the crankcases
verification: Cases apart evenly with no damage to the joint faces.

steps.instruction: Lift the main axle, drive axle, shift drum and the three shift forks out together, tapping the drive axle lightly with a soft hammer. Note where every fork sits and which way it faces. Remove the collar.
steps.title: Remove the gearbox
verification: Gearbox out; fork positions photographed.

steps.instruction: Fit the crankcase separating tool (90890-01135 / YU-01135-B) with suitable bolts and press the crankshaft out of the case. Never drive the crankshaft out with a hammer.
steps.title: Remove the crankshaft
verification: Crank out without damage to the case.

title: First start, break-in, premix and jetting checks after an engine rebuild
completeness: Covers pre-start checks, stock carburetor settings, break-in premix, cold start, idle, the staged break-in, post break-in checks and the first oil change.
critical_stop_conditions: Knocking or pinging: stop and use a different brand or higher octane fuel.
Coolant or oil leaking, coolant level dropping, or steam: stop the engine and find the cause before restarting.
Any new noise, a sudden loss of power or the engine tightening up: stop at once and inspect before running again.
Never mix two different two-stroke oils in one batch; drain the tank and float bowl before switching oils.
entry_state: Yamaha YZ250X with a rebuilt top end or engine fully reassembled and refitted, fluids filled, not yet started.
excluded: Jetting changes for altitude or temperature beyond the stock baseline
exit_state: Engine started, warmed, broken in on the break-in premix, re-torqued and checked, and switched to the normal premix ratio.
prerequisites: Engine fully assembled and all fasteners torqued per the rebuild guides.
Coolant and transmission oil filled and checked.
A well-ventilated outdoor space; never run the engine in a closed area.

required_parts.name: Premium unleaded gasoline (E10 is acceptable)
required_parts.purpose: Fuel for the break-in and normal premix.

required_parts.name: YAMALUBE 2R or equivalent two-stroke oil
Spark plug NGK BR8EG
Foam air filter oil
required_parts.purpose: Air filter service before the first run.

required_parts.name: Transmission oil: Motor oil SAE 10W-40, API service SG or higher, JASO MA
required_parts.purpose: For the oil change after break-in.

required_tools.name: Spark plug socket and wire feeler gauge
Flat screwdriver for the pilot air screw

steps.instruction: Wash the foam filter in filter cleaner or kerosene (never gasoline), squeeze it dry without twisting, and oil it in a bag until it is evenly wet but not dripping. Grease the sealing face of the filter case and refit the element and its guide so it seals all round. Never run the engine without the filter.
steps.title: Service the air filter
verification: Filter oiled, seated and sealing.

steps.instruction: With the bike upright and level, remove the transmission oil check bolt: oil must just flow out (10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft on refit). Check the coolant is at the top of the radiator filler neck.
steps.title: Check the fluids
verification: Oil at the check bolt; coolant full.

steps.instruction: Use an NGK BR8EG spark plug gapped to 0.5–0.6 mm (0.020–0.024 in), clean threads and seat, tighten to 20 N·m (14 lb·ft) and fit the cap.
steps.title: Fit a correctly gapped spark plug
verification: Plug type, gap and torque recorded.

steps.instruction: Confirm the carburetor carries the stock parts: main jet #178, jet needle N3EW-2, pilot jet #50, power jet #50, pilot air screw 1-1/4 turns out. Float height is 6.5 mm (0.26 in). The pilot air screw is set individually at the factory: turn it in until it lightly seats, counting the turns, record that number, then turn it back out the same amount. Set throttle grip free play to 3.0–5.0 mm (0.12–0.20 in) and clutch lever free play to 7.0–12.0 mm (0.28–0.47 in).
steps.title: Confirm the stock carburetor settings
verification: Jet sizes, needle and air screw turns recorded.

title: Full fork service: seals, bushings, oil and damper cartridge oil
completeness: Covers removing both legs, full strip, inspection with limits, damper bleeding and oil level, new seals and bushings, adjuster gap, outer chamber oil and refit.
critical_stop_conditions: Inner tube runout over 0.2 mm (0.01 in): replace the tube; never straighten it.
Deep scratches or a damaged oil lock piece on the inner tube: replace it.
Fork spring shorter than its limit of 449.0 mm (17.68 in): replace it.
Do not remove the locknut from the damper rod: the rod can drop into the damper and not come back out.
The two legs must end up with the same oil level and amount; uneven legs handle badly.
Overtightening the lower bracket pinch bolts can stop the fork working properly: use the torque wrench.
entry_state: Yamaha YZ250X with stock forks fitted, front wheel on.
exit_state: Both fork legs rebuilt with new seals and bushings, damper and outer chamber filled to the stock amounts, refitted at the stock height and torque, clickers back at the recorded settings.
prerequisites: Bike clean, especially the fork tubes.
A clean bench; the fork internals are very sensitive to dirt.
Work on one leg at a time.

required_parts.name: Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (or the same grade)
required_parts.purpose: Damper 205 cm³ (6.93 US oz) plus outer chamber 320 cm³ (10.8 US oz) per leg.

required_parts.name: New oil seals, dust seals, slide metals and piston metals for both legs
required_parts.purpose: Always replaced when the fork is opened.

required_parts.name: New copper washers for the adjusters
Lithium-soap-based grease and medium threadlocker
required_parts.purpose: Seal lips and the adjuster threads.

required_tools.name: Front stand that lifts the front wheel
Oil level gauge or a steel rule and syringe

steps.instruction: Count and record the rebound and compression clicker positions on both legs (turn in to the stop, counting). Note how far the outer tubes stick up above the upper bracket. Lift the front wheel off the ground on a secure stand.
steps.title: Record settings and lift the front
verification: Clicker settings and fork height recorded.

steps.instruction: Remove the front wheel. Unbolt the front brake caliper and hang it without stretching the hose; do not squeeze the brake lever. Remove the number plate and the fork protectors.
steps.title: Remove the front wheel, caliper and guards
verification: Wheel, caliper and protectors off.

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper bracket pinch bolts. Loosen the damper assembly (fork cap) with the cap bolt ring wrench while the leg is still clamped. Support the leg, loosen the lower bracket pinch bolts and slide the leg out.
steps.title: Remove a fork leg
verification: Leg out; cap loosened.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, slide the outer tube down and pour the oil out of the leg into a pan.
steps.title: Drain the fork oil
verification: Oil drained; any metal or debris noted.

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and fit the cap bolt ring wrench between the inner tube and the locknut on the damper rod. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster from the damper rod. Leave the locknut on the rod. Remove the adjuster, the damper adjusting rod, the damper assembly and the fork spring with its upper spring seat.
steps.title: Remove the bottom adjuster
verification: Locknut still on the rod; spring and damper out.

steps.instruction: Prise off the dust seal and remove the stopper ring with a flat screwdriver without scratching the inner tube. Push the inner tube in slowly almost to the bottom, then pull it out sharply; repeat until the tubes separate. Slide the piston metal, slide metal, washer, oil seal and dust seal off the inner tube.
steps.title: Separate the tubes
verification: Tubes apart; old bushings and seals off.

steps.instruction: Record the compression adjuster position and turn it fully out. Hold the damper assembly with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench (YM-01500 / 90890-01500).
steps.title: Remove the base valve
verification: Base valve out; adjuster setting recorded.

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube for scratches (light marks can be smoothed with #1000 wet paper) and a damaged oil lock piece. Measure inner tube runout on V-blocks with a dial gauge; the bend is half the gauge reading (limit 0.2 mm / 0.01 in). Check the outer tube for scratches and wear. Measure fork spring free length (limit 449.0 mm / 17.68 in). Check the damper assembly for bends, the base valve, upper spring seat, adjuster and bleed screw for wear, and all O-rings.
steps.title: Inspect the fork parts
verification: Runout and spring length recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: Pull the damper assembly to full extension and fill it with 205 cm³ (6.93 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1. Pump the rod slowly up and down several times to bleed it, keeping each stroke short of 200 mm (7.9 in). A stroke that long or longer lets air in; if that happens, repeat the fill and bleed.
steps.title: Fill and bleed the damper
verification: Damper bled with no air bubbles.

steps.instruction: With the damper fully extended, measure the oil level from the top of the damper assembly: 145–148 mm (5.71–5.83 in). Add or remove oil to get it right. Screw the locknut fully onto the damper rod by hand.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Damper oil level recorded.

steps.instruction: Push the damper rod in to build pressure, then fit the base valve while letting the rod come back out. Check the damper is fully extended; if not, repeat the fill. Tighten the base valve to 29 N·m (21 lb·ft) with the cap bolt wrench while holding the damper with the ring wrench.
steps.title: Refit the base valve
verification: Base valve torqued; damper fully extended.

steps.instruction: Pump the damper slowly more than 10 times to spread the oil. Wrap it in a cloth, compress it fully and let the extra oil overflow on the base valve side and out of the hole in the damper (about 10 cm³). Check the damper strokes smoothly with no tight or rough spots.
steps.title: Purge the excess damper oil
verification: Damper smooth through its stroke.

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with thin plastic film coated in fork oil. Slide on, in order, a new dust seal, the stopper ring, a new oil seal (numbered side facing down), the washer and a new slide metal. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips and oil the tube. Fit a new piston metal into the slot on the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit new seals and bushings to the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order; oil seal numbers facing down.

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Press the slide metal and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver (YM-A0948 / 90890-01502), then the oil seal until the stopper ring groove is fully visible. Fit the stopper ring fully into its groove and press in the dust seal. Check the tube slides smoothly.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive the seals
verification: Stopper ring seated all round; tubes slide smoothly.

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper assembly to the bottom of the locknut: 16 mm (0.63 in) or more. Turn the locknut to get this distance.
steps.title: Set the locknut on the damper rod
verification: Distance recorded.

steps.instruction: Fit the upper spring seat with its larger diameter toward the spring and the fork spring onto the damper assembly. Lower the damper assembly slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom without hitting the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Damper seated in the inner tube.

steps.instruction: Record and fully loosen the rebound adjuster. Fit the damper adjusting rod, a new copper washer and the adjuster: compress the inner tube, set the ring wrench under the locknut and screw the adjuster onto the damper rod by hand until it stops. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: 0.5–1.0 mm (0.02–0.04 in). Holding the locknut, tighten the adjuster to the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb·ft). Then tighten the adjuster into the inner tube with threadlocker to 55 N·m (40 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the bottom adjuster
verification: Gap recorded; both adjuster torques done.

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 320 cm³ (10.8 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (adjustable range 300–365 cm³ / 10.1–12.3 US oz; use the same amount in both legs). Thread the damper assembly into the outer tube by hand and fit the protector guide.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber
verification: Oil amount recorded.

steps.instruction: Repeat every step for the second leg, using the same amounts and settings.
steps.title: Repeat for the other leg
verification: Both legs rebuilt identically.

steps.instruction: Slide each leg into the clamps with the top of the outer tube level with the top of the upper bracket and snug the lower pinch bolts. Tighten the damper assembly to 30 N·m (22 lb·ft) with the ring wrench. Tighten the upper bracket pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft) and the lower bracket pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Refit the fork protectors (5 N·m / 3.6 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the fork legs
verification: Height equal both sides; all bolts torqued.

steps.instruction: Turn each rebound and compression adjuster in until it stops, then back out to the positions you recorded.
steps.title: Restore the clicker settings
verification: Settings match the record.

steps.instruction: Fit the brake caliper (28 N·m / 20 lb·ft) and the brake hose holder (8 N·m / 5.8 lb·ft), and the number plate. Fit the wheel with the disc between the pads and the axle greased. Pump the fork several times before tightening the axle nut to 105 N·m (75 lb·ft), then the axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Pump the brake lever until it is firm.
steps.title: Refit the wheel and brake
verification: Brake firm; fork moves smoothly with no leaks.

steps.instruction: Count and record the rebound and compression clicker positions on both legs (turn in to the stop, counting). Note how far the outer tubes stick up above the upper bracket. Lift the front wheel off the ground on a secure stand.
steps.title: Record settings and lift the front
verification: Clicker settings and fork height recorded.

steps.instruction: Remove the front wheel. Unbolt the front brake caliper and hang it without stretching the hose; do not squeeze the brake lever. Remove the number plate and the fork protectors.
