verification: Wheel, caliper and protectors off.

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper bracket pinch bolts. Loosen the damper assembly (fork cap) with the cap bolt ring wrench while the leg is still clamped. Support the leg, loosen the lower bracket pinch bolts and slide the leg out.
steps.title: Remove a fork leg
verification: Leg out; cap loosened.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, slide the outer tube down and pour the oil out of the leg into a pan.
steps.title: Drain the fork oil
verification: Oil drained; any metal or debris noted.

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and fit the cap bolt ring wrench between the inner tube and the locknut on the damper rod. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster from the damper rod. Leave the locknut on the rod. Remove the adjuster, the damper adjusting rod, the damper assembly and the fork spring with its upper spring seat.
steps.title: Remove the bottom adjuster
verification: Locknut still on the rod; spring and damper out.

steps.instruction: Prise off the dust seal and remove the stopper ring with a flat screwdriver without scratching the inner tube. Push the inner tube in slowly almost to the bottom, then pull it out sharply; repeat until the tubes separate. Slide the piston metal, slide metal, washer, oil seal and dust seal off the inner tube.
steps.title: Separate the tubes
verification: Tubes apart; old bushings and seals off.

steps.instruction: Record the compression adjuster position and turn it fully out. Hold the damper assembly with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench (90890-01500 / YM-01500).
steps.title: Remove the base valve
verification: Base valve out; adjuster setting recorded.

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube for scratches (light marks can be smoothed with #1000 wet paper) and a damaged oil lock piece. Measure inner tube runout on V-blocks with a dial gauge; the bend is half the gauge reading (limit 0.2 mm / 0.01 in). Check the outer tube for scratches and wear. Measure fork spring free length (limit 449.0 mm / 17.68 in). Check the damper assembly for bends, the base valve, upper spring seat, adjuster and bleed screw for wear, and all O-rings.
steps.title: Inspect the fork parts
verification: Runout and spring length recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: Pull the damper assembly to full extension and fill it with 205 cm³ (6.93 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1. Pump the rod slowly up and down several times to bleed it, keeping each stroke short of 200 mm (7.9 in). A stroke that long or longer lets air in; if that happens, repeat the fill and bleed.
steps.title: Fill and bleed the damper
verification: Damper bled with no air bubbles.

steps.instruction: With the damper fully extended, measure the oil level from the top of the damper assembly: 145–148 mm (5.71–5.83 in). Add or remove oil to get it right. Screw the locknut fully onto the damper rod by hand.
steps.title: Set the damper oil level
verification: Damper oil level recorded.

steps.instruction: Push the damper rod in to build pressure, then fit the base valve while letting the rod come back out. Check the damper is fully extended; if not, repeat the fill. Tighten the base valve to 29 N·m (21 lb·ft) with the cap bolt wrench while holding the damper with the ring wrench.
steps.title: Refit the base valve
verification: Base valve torqued; damper fully extended.

steps.instruction: Pump the damper slowly more than 10 times to spread the oil. Wrap it in a cloth, compress it fully and let the extra oil overflow on the base valve side and out of the hole in the damper (about 10 cm³). Check the damper strokes smoothly with no tight or rough spots.
steps.title: Purge the excess damper oil
verification: Damper smooth through its stroke.

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with thin plastic film coated in fork oil. Slide on, in order, a new dust seal, the stopper ring, a new oil seal (numbered side facing down), the washer and a new slide metal. Grease the dust seal and oil seal lips and oil the tube. Fit a new piston metal into the slot on the inner tube.
steps.title: Fit new seals and bushings to the inner tube
verification: Parts on in the right order; oil seal numbers facing down.

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. Press the slide metal and washer into the outer tube with the fork seal driver (90890-01502 / YM-A0948), then the oil seal until the stopper ring groove is fully visible. Fit the stopper ring fully into its groove and press in the dust seal. Check the tube slides smoothly.
steps.title: Join the tubes and drive the seals
verification: Stopper ring seated all round; tubes slide smoothly.

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper assembly to the bottom of the locknut: 16 mm (0.63 in) or more. Turn the locknut to get this distance.
steps.title: Set the locknut on the damper rod
verification: Distance recorded.

steps.instruction: Fit the upper spring seat with its larger diameter toward the spring and the fork spring onto the damper assembly. Lower the damper assembly slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom without hitting the tube.
steps.title: Fit the spring and damper
verification: Damper seated in the inner tube.

steps.instruction: Record and fully loosen the rebound adjuster. Fit the damper adjusting rod, a new copper washer and the adjuster: compress the inner tube, set the ring wrench under the locknut and screw the adjuster onto the damper rod by hand until it stops. Measure the gap between adjuster and locknut: 0.5–1.0 mm (0.02–0.04 in). Holding the locknut, tighten the adjuster to the locknut at 29 N·m (21 lb·ft). Then tighten the adjuster into the inner tube with threadlocker to 55 N·m (41 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the bottom adjuster
verification: Gap recorded; both adjuster torques done.

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 320 cm³ (10.8 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (adjustable range 300–365 cm³ / 10.1–12.3 US oz; use the same amount in both legs). Thread the damper assembly into the outer tube by hand and fit the protector guide.
steps.title: Fill the outer chamber
verification: Oil amount recorded.

steps.instruction: Repeat every step for the second leg, using the same amounts and settings.
steps.title: Repeat for the other leg
verification: Both legs rebuilt identically.

steps.instruction: Slide each leg into the clamps with the top of the outer tube level with the top of the upper bracket and snug the lower pinch bolts. Tighten the damper assembly to 30 N·m (22 lb·ft) with the ring wrench. Tighten the upper bracket pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft) and the lower bracket pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Refit the fork protectors (5 N·m / 3.7 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the fork legs
verification: Height equal both sides; all bolts torqued.

steps.instruction: Turn each rebound and compression adjuster in until it stops, then back out to the positions you recorded.
steps.title: Restore the clicker settings
verification: Settings match the record.

steps.instruction: Fit the brake caliper (28 N·m / 21 lb·ft) and the brake hose holder (9 N·m / 6.6 lb·ft), and the number plate. Fit the wheel with the disc between the pads and the axle greased. Pump the fork several times before tightening the axle nut to 105 N·m (77 lb·ft), then the axle pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft). Pump the brake lever until it is firm.
steps.title: Refit the wheel and brake
verification: Brake firm; fork moves smoothly with no leaks.

steps.instruction: Remove the front wheel. Unbolt the front brake caliper and hang it without stretching the hose; do not squeeze the brake lever. Remove the number plate and the fork protectors.

steps.instruction: Loosen the upper bracket pinch bolts. Loosen the damper assembly (fork cap) with the cap bolt ring wrench while the leg is still clamped. Support the leg, loosen the lower bracket pinch bolts and slide the leg out.

verification: Leg out; cap loosened.

steps.instruction: Unscrew the damper assembly from the outer tube, slide the outer tube down and pour the oil out of the leg into a pan.

verification: Oil drained; any metal or debris noted.

steps.instruction: Compress the inner tube and fit the cap bolt ring wrench between the inner tube and the locknut on the damper rod. Hold the locknut and unscrew the adjuster from the damper rod. steps.instruction: Prise off the dust seal and remove the stopper ring with a flat screwdriver without scratching the inner tube. steps.instruction: Record the compression adjuster position and turn it fully out. Remove the adjuster knob. Hold the damper assembly with the cap bolt ring wrench and unscrew the base valve with the cap bolt wrench (90890-01911).

verification: Base valve out; adjuster setting recorded.

steps.instruction: Check the inner tube for scratches (light marks can be smoothed with #1000 wet paper) and a damaged oil lock piece. verification: Runout and spring length recorded; parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: Pull the damper assembly to full extension and fill it with 205 cm³ (6.93 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1. Pump the rod slowly up and down several times to bleed it, keeping each stroke short of 200 mm (7.9 in). A stroke that long or longer lets air in; if that happens, repeat the fill and bleed.

verification: Damper bled with no air bubbles.

steps.instruction: With the damper fully extended, measure the oil level from the top of the damper assembly: 145–148 mm (5.71–5.83 in). Add or remove oil to get it right. Screw the locknut fully onto the damper rod by hand.

verification: Damper oil level recorded.

steps.instruction: Push the damper rod in to build pressure, then fit the base valve while letting the rod come back out. Check the damper is fully extended; if not, repeat the fill. verification: Base valve torqued; damper fully extended.

steps.instruction: Pump the damper slowly more than 10 times to spread the oil. Wrap it in a cloth, compress it fully and let the extra oil overflow on the base valve side and out of the hole in the damper (about 10 cm³). Check the damper strokes smoothly with no tight or rough spots.

verification: Damper smooth through its stroke.

steps.instruction: Cover the end of the inner tube with thin plastic film coated in fork oil. Fit a new piston metal into the slot on the inner tube.

verification: Parts on in the right order; oil seal numbers facing down.

steps.instruction: Slide the outer tube onto the inner tube. verification: Stopper ring seated all round; tubes slide smoothly.

steps.instruction: Measure from the bottom of the damper assembly to the bottom of the locknut: 16 mm (0.63 in) or more. Turn the locknut to get this distance.

verification: Distance recorded.

steps.instruction: Fit the upper spring seat with its larger diameter toward the spring and the fork spring onto the damper assembly. Lower the damper assembly slowly into the inner tube until it rests on the bottom without hitting the tube.

steps.instruction: Record and fully loosen the rebound adjuster. verification: Gap recorded; both adjuster torques done.

steps.instruction: Fill the leg with 285 cm³ (9.6 US oz) of Yamaha Suspension Oil S1 (adjustable range 265–365 cm³ / 9.0–12.3 US oz; use the same amount in both legs). Thread the damper assembly into the outer tube by hand and fit the protector guide.

verification: Oil amount recorded.

steps.instruction: Repeat every step for the second leg, using the same amounts and settings.
steps.title: Repeat for the other leg
verification: Both legs rebuilt identically.

steps.instruction: Slide each leg into the clamps with the top of the outer tube level with the top of the upper bracket and snug the lower pinch bolts. verification: Height equal both sides; all bolts torqued.

steps.instruction: Turn each rebound and compression adjuster in until it stops, then back out to the positions you recorded.

verification: Settings match the record.

steps.instruction: Fit the brake caliper (28 N·m / 21 lb·ft) and the brake hose holder (9 N·m / 6.6 lb·ft), and the number plate. Fit the wheel with the disc between the pads and the axle greased. steps.instruction: With the pivot shaft nut at 85 N·m (61 lb·ft), move the swingarm side to side and up and down. Side play or rough, binding movement points to worn bearings, bushings or collars.

verification: Play and smoothness recorded.

verification: Wheel out; pullers and collars bagged.

verification: Linkage arms out; bolts bagged by position.

verification: Swingarm off; engine still supported.

verification: Parts laid out by location; depths noted.

steps.instruction: Clean everything in kerosene. Roll the pivot shaft on a flat surface; a bend means replace. Check the swingarm and arms for cracks and bends. Any free play, rough turning or rust in a bearing, bushing or collar means replace them as a set.

verification: Parts to replace listed.

steps.instruction: Grease with molybdenum disulfide grease. Press the outer needle bearings in first, then the inner ones, working from the inside to the set depths: depth a 0 mm (0 in), depth b 6.5 mm (0.26 in). Fit the new oil seals, bushings, thrust bearings and collars.

verification: Depths measured and recorded.

steps.instruction: Grease the bearings, washers, seals and collars with molybdenum disulfide grease. Press the bearings into the relay arm (installed depth 0 mm / 0 in) and the connecting arm (installed depth 0 mm / 0 in), then fit new oil seals and the collars.

verification: Depths recorded; collars turn smoothly.

steps.instruction: Grease the pivot shaft. Fit the swingarm and push the pivot shaft in from the right, through the swingarm and engine. Tighten the pivot shaft nut to 85 N·m (61 lb·ft).

verification: Pivot nut torqued; swingarm moves smoothly with no side play.

steps.instruction: Grease all linkage bolts (shank and thread) with molybdenum disulfide grease. steps.title: Fit the linkage
verification: All linkage nuts torqued.

verification: Slack recorded; axle and locknuts torqued; brake firm.

title: Service or replace the steering head bearings
completeness: Covers removing the forks and lower bracket, inspecting and replacing bearings and races, greasing and setting the ring nut preload.

steps.instruction: With the front wheel off the ground, grasp the bottom of the forks and rock them back and forth, then turn the bars lock to lock. Note any knock, notch or tight spot.

verification: Lower bracket out without dropping the lower bearing.

branches.condition: No pitting, dents or rough spots on any bearing or race.

verification: New races fully seated and square.

steps.instruction: Pack both bearings and coat the races with lithium-soap-based grease, and grease the dust seal lip. Fit the lower bearing on the stem, the upper bearing and race cover in the head tube, grease the stem thread, and push the stem up into the head tube.

steps.instruction: Fit the ring nut with its stepped side facing down. Using the steering nut wrench with the torque wrench at a right angle to it, tighten the ring nut to about 38 N·m (27 lb·ft). steps.title: Set the bearing preload
verification: Both ring nut torques done; stem turns smoothly with no play.

steps.instruction: Fit the washer, slide the fork legs into both brackets with the outer tubes level with the top of the upper bracket, snug the lower pinch bolts and fit the upper bracket. Grease the face of the stem nut and tighten it to 145 N·m (105 lb·ft). Turn the steering lock to lock; if it is tight, back off the ring nut a little at a time until it is smooth. Tighten the upper pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft) and the lower pinch bolts to 21 N·m (15 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit the upper bracket and forks
verification: Stem nut and pinch bolts torqued; fork height equal.

steps.instruction: Fit the handlebar (upper holder bolts 28 N·m / 20 lb·ft; lower holder nuts 40 N·m / 29 lb·ft if they were removed), the front fender (10 N·m / 7.2 lb·ft), number plate, caliper (28 N·m / 20 lb·ft) and hose holder (8 N·m / 5.8 lb·ft). steps.title: Refit the front end
verification: Everything torqued.

steps.instruction: Turn the bars lock to lock: smooth, no notches, no cable or hose pulling. Rock the fork for play. Pump the brake lever until firm.
steps.title: Check steering and brake
verification: Smooth steering, no play, brake firm.

title: Replace the front wheel bearings and seals

steps.instruction: Lift the front, loosen the axle pinch bolts, remove the axle nut and axle and lower the wheel out. Keep the collars. Do not squeeze the brake lever.

verification: Wheel and collars off.

steps.instruction: Clean the hub. Lever the oil seals out with a flat screwdriver over a rag to protect the hub. Pull the bearings out with a bearing puller.

verification: Seals and bearings out; spacer kept.

steps.instruction: Roll the axle on a flat surface to check for bends (limit 0.50 mm / 0.02 in). Check the collars for wear and the hub bores for damage.

steps.instruction: Press in the left side bearing first, then the spacer and the other bearing, pushing only on the outer race with a socket the size of the race, keeping each bearing square. Fit new oil seals with their markings facing out and grease the lips. If the disc was removed, refit it with threadlocker on the bolts and tighten them in a crisscross pattern to 12 N·m (8.7 lb·ft).
steps.title: Fit new bearings and seals
verification: Bearings flush and square; seals in; disc torqued if removed.

steps.instruction: Grease the seal lips and fit the collars with their projections toward the wheel. Fit the wheel with the disc between the pads and slide in the greased axle. steps.title: Refit the wheel
verification: Axle nut and pinch bolts torqued.

steps.instruction: Spin the wheel and measure radial and lateral runout at the rim (limit 2.0 mm / 0.08 in each). Pump the brake lever until firm.
steps.title: Check runout and brake
verification: Runout recorded; brake firm.
